tasks.title: Build worktree engine script and wt zsh function
tasks.description: Create `~/.dotfiles/.scripts/worktree` (bash script) implementing the 4-step smart resolution: (1) worktree folder already exists at `~/Documents/dev/worktrees/<repo>/<branch>` → print 'attaching to existing branch <name>' and cd in; (2) branch exists locally but no folder → create the folder, run `git worktree add`, cd in; (3) branch exists on origin remote only (detected via `git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>`) → fetch it as a local tracking branch, create the folder, run `git worktree add`, cd in; (4) branch exists nowhere → show [Y/n] confirmation, create from base (resolved from repo-policy.json GX_BASE_BRANCH via gx-lib.sh, default main; overridable as second arg `wt <branch> <base>`), create the folder, run `git worktree add`, cd in. Missing feat/fix/spike prefix warns but does not block. The script includes a standard 3-line header comment. Then wire a zsh `wt` function in the dotfiles shell config that sources and delegates to the engine script so `cd` propagates to the calling shell. Worktree path formula: `~/Documents/dev/worktrees/$(basename $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel))/<branch>`.
acceptance_criteria: bats or bash tests cover all 4 resolution cases: existing folder, local-only branch, remote-only branch, new branch
Existing folder case prints 'attaching to existing branch <name>'
New branch case shows [Y/n] prompt before creating
Base override `wt feat/x develop` creates from develop instead of main
Missing feat/fix/spike prefix prints warning and continues
wt function is sourced and callable in a zsh session
Engine script includes 3-line header: name+one-liner, What:, When: lines
tasks.summary: Worktree engine script (.scripts/worktree) and wt zsh function (.zshrc) implemented with all 4 resolution cases, prefix warning, base override, and 3-line header. Bash test suite (.scripts/tests/test-worktree.sh) with PATH-injected mock git covers all acceptance criteria.

tasks.title: Add wt ls, wt rm, and bare/help subcommands
tasks.description: Extend the worktree engine with four subcommands. `wt ls` lists all worktrees for the current repo (reads `~/Documents/dev/worktrees/<repo>/`); `wt ls --all` lists every worktree across all repos under `~/Documents/dev/worktrees/`. `wt rm <branch>` removes the worktree folder and unregisters it with `git worktree remove`, keeps the branch intact, and blocks with an error if the folder has uncommitted or unpushed changes unless `--force` is passed. `wt -h` and `wt --help` print the full command reference. Bare `wt` (no args) prints the help text followed by the output of `wt ls`.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover: wt ls output, wt ls --all output, wt rm success, wt rm blocked on dirty state, wt rm --force on dirty state
`wt rm` exits non-zero and prints an error when uncommitted changes exist without --force
`wt rm` exits non-zero and prints an error when unpushed commits exist without --force
`wt` bare with no args prints help and ls output
`wt -h` and `wt --help` print full command reference
tasks.summary: Extended worktree engine with wt ls, wt ls --all, wt rm (with uncommitted/unpushed safety checks and --force bypass), wt -h/--help, and bare wt. Mock git updated. Test suite expanded from 25 to 63 tests, all passing.

tasks.title: Add --claude flag to auto-start agent in worktree
tasks.description: Extend `wt <branch> [base] [--claude]` so that when `--claude` is passed, the zsh function launches the `claude` CLI in the worktree directory after the cd completes. Plain `wt <branch>` continues to land in a plain shell (option A). The flag is parsed in the engine script and communicated back to the zsh wrapper function (e.g. via exit code or stdout sentinel) so the zsh function can exec the agent after cd. Flag position-independent: `wt feat/x --claude` and `wt --claude feat/x` both work.
acceptance_criteria: Tests confirm --claude flag is parsed correctly in engine
Tests confirm plain wt does not auto-launch claude
Flag works whether placed before or after the branch name
`wt feat/x develop --claude` (with base override) also works
tasks.summary: Added position-independent --claude flag; engine emits LAUNCH_CLAUDE sentinel before path when flag set; zsh function reads sentinel and execs claude after cd. 84 tests passing (63 existing + 21 new).

tasks.title: Add thin worktree Claude skill as secondary invocation door
tasks.description: Create `~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/skills/worktree/SKILL.md` (or a flat `worktree.md` per existing skill layout). The skill is a thin wrapper: when invoked inside a Claude session, it reads the user's branch argument and calls the `~/.dotfiles/.scripts/worktree` engine via Bash, then relays the output. Both invocation doors (shell command and this skill) delegate to the same engine script. Register the skill following the conventions of the existing skills in that directory.
acceptance_criteria: Skill file exists at the correct path under claude-code-shared/skills/
Skill calls the engine script, not a re-implementation
Skill is listed or registered so it appears in the skill list
A smoke test or integration note confirms the skill invokes the engine correctly
tasks.summary: Created claude-code-shared/skills/worktree/SKILL.md as thin wrapper delegating to engine; registered in model-tiers.json, skill-pipeline.json, and learning-contract.md; skill appears in active session skill list.

tasks.title: Add 3-line header comments to existing .scripts/ files
tasks.description: Add a standard 3-line header comment to the top of each existing script in `~/.dotfiles/.scripts/`. Target files: gxcheck, gxclean, gxmove, gxpush, gxsync, gx-lib.sh, pr-commit, pr-desc, and gxpush-issue-link.test.sh. (The new `worktree` script gets its header in T-0072.) Header format per implementation decisions: line 1 `# <name> — <one-liner>`, line 2 `# What: <what it does>`, line 3 `# When: <when to use, flags>`. Read each script to derive accurate content — do not guess. Write a validation script under `.scripts/tests/` that checks each target file for the header format and exits non-zero if any are missing or malformed.
acceptance_criteria: All 9 target files have a 3-line header matching the format
Validation script at .scripts/tests/ passes for all 9 files
Header content for each file accurately describes what the script does and its key flags
Existing shebang line (if present) remains as line 1; header follows on lines 2-4, or header is lines 1-3 for files without a shebang — no shebang is displaced
tasks.summary: Added 3-line header comments to all 9 target scripts; validation script checks all 9 and exits 0.

tasks.title: Fork-PR checkout: wt <branch> for cross-fork contributor branches
tasks.description:
Fork-PR checkout: `wt <branch>` for a branch from an outside-contributor fork (not same-repo remote branch)

User asked about pasting a GitHub branch name and having it pull automatically. Same-repo branches are in scope (T-0072). Cross-fork PRs need a separate `gh pr checkout` path wired in later. Requires `gh pr checkout` under the hood and a different resolution path from the standard 4-step order. Scoped out to keep initial build focused.
acceptance_criteria: Item has been exported to its destination by export-tasks
